entries.name: The Letter (Aletheion Heist)
entries.summary: The anonymous letter that sets [[The Aletheion Heist]] in motion.
entries.body:
You were named to me three times, by three mouths, and so I write. There is a house on Museum Hill where the city keeps its memory, and in that house one small thing that is mine by an older claim than any label. Tomorrow it goes where no claim can follow. Tonight, then.

Six hundred gold when we speak. Nine hundred more when it rests in my hand, three hundred a head for five, half again a fair rate, because the house is careful and I am generous. Everything the work requires has already been bought and paid for; you will simply be collecting it. Come to the revel beneath the Old Harbor when the drums start. Wear a mask. Bring a truth you can bear to say aloud, the door charges one.

My circle asks three things. Kill no one. Be seen taking nothing. And whatever you find at the heart of that house, do not touch it with your skin. — T.

entries.name: (印章) Yinzhang
entries.summary: Fairy Wizard 4
entries.body:
Yinzhang is a medium-sized male fairy and a gifted wizard, born with a dangerous secret: he shares his body with a second, darker mind named Yangzhang. Where Yinzhang is anxious, kind, and bookish, Yangzhang is cold, calculating, and frighteningly composed. The two are not separate personalities—they are two minds trapped in one body, always conscious, always watching. When tensions rise, when voices raise, or even when fear creeps in, Yangzhang breaks through. He doesn’t possess; he overwhelms. Magic flares, words turn to blades, and those around Yinzhang often pay the price. After Yangzhang incinerated a ceremonial shrine in a fit of calm cruelty, their hometown exiled them both. Only one person remained kind—Zhangyin, his eccentric and battle-happy cousin. She never judged him, never flinched. But during their separate journeys to Asetheria, the two were split apart. She vanished somewhere along the way. Now, Yinzhang wanders alone, desperately searching for Zhangyin—not just to reunite with his only family, but because her presence is the only thing that’s ever truly quieted Yangzhang’s voice.

entries.name: Haver de Fraudre
entries.summary: Reborn Paladin 4
entries.body:
died with mercy on my blade — I rose with none in my chest."

Haver de Fruadre was once known as Haver the Enlightened, a radiant noble prepared from birth to carry the sacred lineage of the Great Anubis — a divine bloodline said to bring peace to the dead and judgment to the wicked. She was poised to become the next Heir of the Jackal Crown, a living symbol of balance between life and death.

But in a world where power is coveted, legends become targets.

A secret cabal, obsessed with immortality, spread the myth that drinking the blood of Anubis’s true descendantscould grant eternal youth or restore the dead to life. Though untrue, this belief led to centuries of hunting the bloodline — and Haver, the most visible heir, was always in their sights.

What few knew was that Haver had a younger sister, Sca’meyr, hidden away by the family under the guise of being a distant relative. She bore the same divine blood — but not the public title, not the expectation. She was hidden to survive.

---

## 🐺 The Fall

Haver was trained as a priestess of protection — a swordbearer sworn never to strike in hatred, only to shield. But that vow was broken when the enemies of their house launched a massacre disguised as a diplomatic gathering.

It was no parley — it was a slaughter.

Haver held the gates. She held the line.

But she did not kill when she had the chance.

And the man she spared murdered her younger brother.

Wracked with guilt and consumed by rage, Haver forsook her oath.

She broke the covenant of mercy.

And in the chaos of the final defense, she was struck down — not as a saint, but as a sister weeping over her brother’s body.

She was declared dead.

Five years passed.

---

## 🕯️ The Rebirth

Haver awoke in stone and dust, her once-golden blood now cooled and still. Whatever force restored her — divine backlash, a shattered death pact, or her own hate — she did not come back whole.

She returned a Reborn, stripped of light, armored in memory, and armed with purpose.

She learned that Sca’meyr survived, hidden still, and untouched by the bloodhunt — for now. Their family, trying to protect Sca’meyr from both prophecy and politics, had cut ties and covered her origins.

But Haver remembers. She knows the truth.

And now, with the patience of the grave and the vengeance of a knight, she walks again. She is death to the liars who hunt her kind.

"I’ll send them screaming to my grandsire’s gate —

where jackals feast and sins await.

No crown, no coin will buy them grace;

their souls will rot in Anubis’ face."

​​⚖️ The Oath of the Jackal Gate (Broken)

“I swear by the Gate and by the Judge beyond,

to guard the innocent, speak no wrath, and draw no blade in hate.

Let my strength be a shield, and my voice be a warning.

May those who cross the gate pass clean, or not at all.”

---

### 🩸 But now, twisted by death and grief, her new words are:

“That oath is ash.

Now I swear by bone, by silence, and by blood:

I will shield what light remains by drowning out the dark.

The gate no longer judges — I do.”

entries.name: Sca’meyr de Faudre
entries.summary: Aasimar Cleric 4 (fallen)
entries.body:
Backstory

Sca’meyr de Faudre is an Aasimar born of divine lineage—the daughter of the grandson of Anubis, god of the afterlife. Though blessed with celestial blood and healing power, her path is far from holy tradition. Chaotic and free-spirited, Sca’meyr sees life and death as cycles to be bent, not followed. Raised in a secluded temple, she studied ancient rites and divine balance, but always questioned authority and embraced unorthodox methods.

She now walks the world as a Life Cleric, wielding divine magic to heal allies, disrupt enemies, and challenge rigid truths with flexible faith. While she honors her ancestry, she does not worship it—she forges her own path with divine grace and a trickster’s touch.

Fun fact: Sca’meyr is a distant ancestor of Truth Danotfalse, a bard of some fame in Cindermore, known for blurring the lines between honesty and illusion—a trait clearly passed down.

entries.name: Silvyre
entries.summary: Half-Elf Ranger 4
entries.body:
Silvyre was born in a small forested village with an elven mother and a human father. While her mother was always seemingly away, according to her father, Silv learned to enjoy exploring the woods. Her father eventually taught her the ways of the bow to help him hunt. As she wandered around, she came across Pon, a human boy who always got himself into wacky hijinks. Despite this, the two grew close, even if Silv had to get Pon out of probably dangerous situations. While Silv was curious, Pon was more than that and always seemed eager about ancient artefacts.

One day, the two stumbled upon an old shrine, and Pon seemed too eager to invite Silv to inspect an artefact inside. Before Silv could have a moment to process anything, long, slithery creatures started wrapping around her chest, limbs, and neck, almost suffocating her. She hadn't realised that Pon had disappeared. After some time, she felt like she could move again, but the creatures did not leave her body. Silvyre returned to her village hoping to find Pon there, but she was only met with gasps and shouts, shuns and yelps at what surrounded her. Her father could only stare, and she knew then she couldn't stay any more.

Silvyre is now left wandering and wondering. What had happened to her, or Pon? It almost seemed suspicious. But with nowhere to go, she could only try to survive for herself, and her newfound companions. Perhaps Silv will find clues, and maybe Pon himself, and see whether she'd take revenge or accept forgiveness.

entries.name: Thorfinn Hugrakkur
entries.summary: Mountain Dwarf Barbarian 4
entries.body:
While not a royal member of a dwarven kingdom, you belonged to a once-prominent clan that lived deep within the mountain of Kharveth. During the great Continental War, the mountain was decimated—now nothing more than a broken remnant of its former glory. Many scholars have since tried to locate where Kharveth once stood, but it was destroyed beyond recognition, and those who knew its whereabouts perished long ago. Few even remember the clan Hugrakkur; only a handful remain.

A clan heirloom—a mysterious slate of unknown stone, carved with a face that eerily resembles your own—has been passed down through your bloodline. The slate changes its visage with each new heir, yet always retains something familiar. You know, vaguely, the hidden truth: while the warriors of your clan were away, an 'allied' orc clan turned on you, invading and ravaging your mountain home.

Your ancestors, once vassals to the Imperium, were never true citizens—nomads in allegiance, not in nation. Thorfinn Hugrakkur, one of the last of your blood, lived among the Bloodaxes for a time, but has now left for the [[Duneforged Citadel]].

entries.name: 章音 (Zhāngyīn)
entries.summary: Fairy Monk 4 (fallen)
entries.body:
Zhangyin was born beneath a still, silver moon in the high cradle of the Shenzhan Mountains, where the air grows thin and the wind carries no sound. There, in a world of stone and silence, the Hollow Wind Monastery stood—an ancient sanctuary where monks trained their bodies into scripture and their minds into mirrors. Zhangyin was the monastery’s only fairy initiate in centuries. Small, winged, and entirely too loud. While others meditated in stillness, she preferred movement—both of body and of mouth.

Though trained to restrain her strikes, nothing ever restrained her speech. She spoke constantly, and always with a vocabulary that stretched far beyond her years. Her sentences bloomed with poetic structure and abstract comparison, drifting often into elaborate musings that sounded wise but led nowhere at all. It was not uncommon for Zhangyin to finish sparring an opponent only to launch into a three-minute monologue on how “the curvature of a wrist reflects the inevitability of collapse in all temporary things.” She spoke like a philosopher—but wasn’t one. Her wisdom was spontaneous, self-indulgent, and occasionally nonsensical. Still, her skill was undeniable.

Zhangyin fought with a dancer’s grace and a hammer’s resolve. Her hands could silence chaos. Her presence could soothe wild beasts. But it was her words—lavish, persistent, and laced with strange metaphors—that no one could escape. When war crept toward the mountain’s edge, she left the monastery with no fanfare. She served as a soldier in conflicts not of her making, delivering mercy and ruin in equal measure.

Those who fought beside her either adored her or fled the sound of her approaching soliloquies. Now, with the fighting behind her and her fists at rest, Zhangyin has taken to wandering. With no divine vision, no purpose to fulfill, and certainly no war to fight, she set her sights on Asetheria. No one asked her why she was going.

No one needed to. “Even the stone must stretch eventually,” she said, packing her things. “Perhaps in movement I shall discover the vocabulary of stillness. Or maybe I’ll just enjoy a good pastry.” In truth, it may simply be a vacation. But for Asetheria, a land unprepared for her stream of verbose observations and piercing roundhouse kicks, nothing will ever be the same again.

entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [ ] Locate Veris's Rendezvous Point: Meet the hooded traveler at the agreed-upon location in the outskirts of Duneforged.
- [ ] Escort Veris to Ephelanum: Guide Veris safely through the plains  and past plains predator/bandits.
- [ ] Reach the Designated Point within the Ruins: Accompany Veris to his specific destination within the ancient ruins.
- [ ] Ensure Veris's Objective is Met: Assist Veris in whatever task he needs to complete at the site, or ensure he is able to complete it
- [ ] Return from the Ruins: Safely escort Veris, or yourselves if he departs, out of the perilous ruins.

entries.name: Bandits at the Broken Gate
entries.summary: Quartermaster Thestun is fuming. A vital shipment of rare, iridescent metals intended for Citadel armories was ambushed at Broken Gate Pass, a notorious bottleneck several days' ride west. The bandits, led by a ruthle…
entries.body:
_Offered by [[Thestun Vulkrim]]._

Quartermaster Thestun is fuming. A vital shipment of rare, iridescent metals intended for Citadel armories was ambushed at Broken Gate Pass, a notorious bottleneck several days' ride west. The bandits, led by a ruthless individual known as "The Jackal," have made the pass a no-go zone for honest merchants. Thestun needs a skilled team to reclaim the stolen goods, eliminate The Jackal and his crew, and re-secure the pass for future trade.
entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [ ] Reach Broken Gate Pass: Travel to the known ambush site several days northof the Citadel.
- [ ] Eliminate The Jackal's Crew: Engage and defeat the bandit forces occupying the pass.
- [ ] Confront and Defeat The Jackal: Neutralize the bandit leader.
- [ ] Recover the Stolen Shipment: Locate and secure the crate of iridescent metals.
- [ ] Return to Quartermaster Thestun: Deliver the recovered shipment and confirm the pass is clear.

entries.name: Echoes in the Dune Mines
entries.summary: Deep tremors and a low, unsettling hum have brought mining operations to a halt in the lower shafts of the [[The Dune Mines|Dune Mines]]. The Overseer is growing desperate, his crew on edge, fearing an ancient evil ha…
entries.body:
_Offered by [[Overseer Tarnak]]._

Deep tremors and a low, unsettling hum have brought mining operations to a halt in the lower shafts of the [[The Dune Mines|Dune Mines]]. The Overseer is growing desperate, his crew on edge, fearing an ancient evil has been awakened. He needs a competent group to descend into the depths, investigate the source of the disturbances, and neutralize whatever threat lies within, ensuring the mine can resume its vital operations. Tarnak believes the tremors are too profound for natural causes and worries about the integrity of the entire mine.
entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [ ] Descend to the Lower Shafts: Navigate the unstable mine tunnels to reach the source of the tremors.
- [ ] Investigate the Disturbance: Determine the cause of the unsettling hum and tremors within the deep mines.
- [ ] Neutralize the Threat: Confront and eliminate whatever entity or phenomenon is disrupting mining operations.
- [ ] Report to Overseer: Return to Tarnak with findings and confirmation the mine is safe.

entries.name: The Unknown Signal
entries.summary: Without warning, a colossal pillar of light, or perhaps a strange, pulsating beacon, has erupted far beyond known territory, illuminating the night sky even from the Citadel. No maps record what lies in that direction…
entries.body:
_Offered by Beacon._

Without warning, a colossal pillar of light, or perhaps a strange, pulsating beacon, has erupted far beyond known territory, illuminating the night sky even from the Citadel. No maps record what lies in that direction, and no trade routes pass that way. The source is entirely unknown. The light or ebacon looks to be near or inside the [[The Shattered Pass|Shattered Pass]].
entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [ ] Journey into the Uncharted Pass: Travel towards the colossal pillar of light beyond known territories.
- [ ] Locate the Signal's Source: Pinpoint the exact origin of the phenomenon.
- [ ] Investigate the Phenomenon: Determine the nature of the signal – is it a relic, a living entity, a natural event, or something else entirely?
- [ ] Gather Information/Samples: Collect any data, artifacts, or specimens related to the signal.
- [ ] Report Findings to the Citadel: Return to the Citadel and relay your discoveries to interested scholars or authorities.

entries.name: Time God's Mission
entries.summary: You were approached—perhaps in a dream, perhaps in a moment the world forgot—with a message from a stranger cloaked in stillness. Their words were clear, urgent, and impossible to forget:
entries.body:
You were approached—perhaps in a dream, perhaps in a moment the world forgot—with a message from a stranger cloaked in stillness. Their words were clear, urgent, and impossible to forget:

> "Time is bleeding. There are places that never were, yet still are. You must find them. Seal them. Before all that is becomes all that was."

They spoke of Timerifts—places lost in history, or perhaps torn out of it entirely. Ruins, temples, towns—sometimes spoken of in passing, sometimes remembered by no one at all. These places flicker in and out of reality, leaving behind only confusion and the faint sense that something is wrong.

You have been chosen—not by name, but by fate. Something, or someone, has tampered with the timeline, allowing echoes of forgotten or forbidden places to emerge. These rifts must be found and closed before the damage spreads.
entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [failed] Locate the a Timerift, a site that contradicts all known history
- [ ]  Follow rumors and strange phenomena to track down other Timerifts
- [ ] Uncover the origin and purpose of the Timerifts—and who opened them
- [ ] Witness moments that were erased or rewritten, and decide whether they should remain
- [ ] Choose between restoration and mercy—correct history, or allow peaceful lies to remain
- [ ] Find the Root Rift, and confront the force that dares rewrite time itself

entries.name: Voices from the Far Grass
entries.summary: Kelvar, a grizzled old scout with eyes that have seen too much, speaks of a phenomenon that chills him to the bone: voices carried on the winds from a place few have mapped and even fewer return from. He cannot pinpoi…
entries.body:
_Offered by [[Kelvar]]._

Kelvar, a grizzled old scout with eyes that have seen too much, speaks of a phenomenon that chills him to the bone: voices carried on the winds from a place few have mapped and even fewer return from. He cannot pinpoint the exact location, only that it lies "far beyond the outer plains." He urgently needs a team to journey into this desolate, unmapped territory, find the source of these ethereal voices, and determine their nature – are they a threat, a warning, or something even stranger?
entries.dmNotes:
**Objectives not yet revealed to the party:**

- [ ] Venture Beyond the Outer Plains: Travel into the desolate, unmapped territory Kelvar described.
- [ ] Locate the Source of the Voices: Pinpoint the origin of the ethereal whispers carried on the wind.
- [ ] Determine the Nature of the Voices: Investigate whether the voices are a threat, a warning, or something else.
- [ ] Collect Evidence/Information: Gather any tangible proof or understanding of the phenomenon.
- [ ] Report Findings to Kelvar (and Scholars): Return to Kelvar with your discoveries, and potentially to Citadel scholars.

entries.body:
You have proven your worth as an adventurer. You are able to discern the martial prowess of your enemy. Once on each of your turns you are able to do a free martial check that will have to pass a certain dc. If you succeed, you will get certain benefits.

-Figure out the different skillsets of your enemy

-See if you can Identify its AC, HP or Movement Speed

-Track its intentions next round

Having proficiency in investigation let's you add your investigation modifier to the roll

entries.name: Precision Strike
entries.summary: Adding Tactical Depth to Every Strike With Minor Crit Effects
entries.body:
## ⚔️ Precision Strike Location Table ⚔️

_Adding Tactical Depth to Every Strike With Minor Crit Effects_

---

## 📖 Introduction

When a warrior finds the perfect opening on an archer's shot or a blade strike, the **location of impact** can dramatically alter the flow of battle. This system adds tactical depth to exceptional attacks without slowing down regular combat.

## 🎲 How to Use This Table

- Roll **4d10** on this table whenever an attack exceeds the target’s AC by 5 or more, or when you score a **critical hit**.
- Optional: Also use this when monsters or NPCs score critical hits or use signature strikes.

## 🎯 Why Precision Strikes Matter

Exceptional attacks deserve exceptional results. Rather than every hit feeling identical, this system ensures that **skillful strikes and lucky shots** create memorable tactical moments that shift the tide of battle.

---

## 📌 Enhanced Hit Location Table (4d10)

| Roll | Location | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | Achilles Tendon | The creature falls prone and their speed is reduced by 15 feet until they finish a short rest. |
| 5 | Ankle | The creature’s speed is reduced by 15 feet until the end of their next turn. |
| 6-7 | Shin/Knee | The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fall prone. |
| 8-9 | Lower Leg | The creature’s speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of their next turn. |
| 10 | Upper Leg | The creature must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or have their speed reduced by 5 feet until the end of their next turn. |
| 12 | Hip | The creature has disadvantage on their next attack roll. |
| 13 | Off-Hand | If the creature is holding something in their off-hand, they must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or drop it. |
| 15 | Weapon | The creature has disadvantage on their next attack roll. |
| 16 | Hand | The creature cannot make opportunity attacks until the start of their next turn. |
| 17 | Forearm | The creature cannot make opportunity attacks until the start of their next turn. |
| 18 | Solid Hit | **No additional effect.** The strike lands decisively without complication. |
| 27 | Lower Ribs | The creature cannot take the Dash action on their next turn. |
| 28 | Side/Flank | The creature loses 5 feet of movement speed until the end of their next turn. |
| 30 | Upper Torso | The creature cannot take reactions until the start of their next turn. |
| 31 | Shoulder | The creature cannot make opportunity attacks until the start of their next turn. |
| 33 | Throat/Neck | The creature cannot cast spells with verbal components until the start of their next turn. |
| 36 | Jaw | The creature cannot speak until the start of their next turn. |
| 37 | Face | The creature has disadvantage on Perception checks until the end of their next turn. |
| 39 | Temple | The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of their next turn. |
| 40 | Critical Skull | The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious until the start of their next turn. On a success, they are stunned until the start of their next turn. |
